_comment: Copy to dashboard.config.json (gitignored) and fill in the paths for your
machine. Every key is OPTIONAL: with no config file at all the dashboard
still builds and serves -- the features that need a path disable
themselves and say which key to set, rather than guessing or crashing.
This is the whole config surface; the dashboard reads no key that is not
listed below.
Precedence for every key:  environment variable  >  this file  >  default.
The variable is the key in upper case -- $TRAINING_ROOT, $REVIEW_MIN_PX --
except for five that carry a DASHBOARD_ prefix instead: work_dir,
image_dir, grid_csv, proxies and hide_regions, so $DASHBOARD_WORK_DIR.
Four of the plain names are variables other tools in this repo already
honour, so a single export configures all of them:
sweep_python   -> $SWEEP_PYTHON     (also read by tools/detect/sweep.py)
dogbin_dataset -> $DOGBIN_DATASET   (also read by eval_dogbin.py and
build_review_set.py)
training_root  -> $TRAINING_ROOT    (also read by training_tracker.py,
run_mistakes.py, gate_store.py and
build_dogdet_v3.py)
comet_env_file -> $COMET_ENV_FILE   (also read by fetch_confusion.py and
best_models.py)
Nothing secret belongs here -- API keys live in the repo-root .env.
_work_dir: Where the collector writes its outputs. Only used to build the copy-pasteable per-region commands shown in the UI, and to locate grid_runs when data/data_root.txt is absent. Unset renders as '<work-dir>'.
_image_dir: Download target for new images, again only for the generated commands. Unset renders as '<image-dir>'.
_grid_csv: Grid definition named in the generated commands. The default is almost certainly what you want.
_proxies: Proxy list named in the generated coverage-audit command. Default 'proxies.txt' (gitignored at the repo root).
_hide_regions: Regions the dashboard does not draw -- no card, no bar, no map marker, no entry in any region list. Display only: the catalog, the harvest, the sweep and every generated command still know about them, and nothing here deletes a row. Defaults to Arctic and Antarctica, which between them carry 130 manifest rows, no downloaded images and no ground animals at all. An empty list reads as unset and falls back to that default.
_sweep_python: Interpreter for the detection sweep -- it needs torch, TensorRT and ultralytics, which the dashboard itself does not. Defaults to the interpreter running the dashboard, which is correct for a single-env checkout.
_training_root: The directory holding the ultralytics project folders -- a folder per project, a run directory per training inside it. No default and no guess: on this kind of box the runs live in a separate repo. Unset, the entire Training section says so -- live card, curves, history, run comparison, what-it-got-wrong and the confusion matrices. It also resolves the relative weights path recorded in data/best_models.json, so the dog-bin guesser and the gate pass need it too.
_training_hide_projects: Project folder names the training panel should not list, matched case-insensitively. A folder that once held work and no longer represents a live project is still on disk, and nothing in the run files marks it dead -- so which ones to retire is a judgement rather than a constant shipped to everyone who clones this. Empty by default: every project under training_root is listed. A comma-separated string works as well as a list.
_training_min_epochs: Fewest epochs a finished run needs before it belongs in the history. A run that finished one epoch is a smoke test, not a result -- two of them sat beside 300-epoch runs with a best epoch of 1 and a metric nobody should compare against anything. Default 2; 0 keeps every run. A run that is still training is always shown, however few epochs it has.
mistakes_python: <path to a python with ultralytics, for scoring a run against its val split>
confusion_python: <path to a python with comet_ml, for confusion-matrix fetches>
_dogbin_dataset: Built dog/not_dog crop dataset, used only by the review page's balance tracker. No default: unset, the panel says so. The directory is expected to hold train/{dog,not_dog} and val/{dog,not_dog}.
_review_extra_dir: A second crop directory the review page serves alongside the rolling recent_crops pool. That pool keeps the newest 3,000 and prunes everything else unreviewed; build_review_set.py picks from the WHOLE store instead -- confidence band, size floor, spread over cells -- and writes here, where nothing prunes them. Same filename convention, so the flag ledgers, /hq, the box editor and the country filter all work untouched. A relative path is resolved against the repo, never the working directory, because the server is started from wherever. Unset, the page serves the rolling pool alone.
_review_min_px: Shortest side, in ORIGINAL pixels, a detection box must have before its crop is offered for review. A 17x15 box in a 1920x1080 frame is ~255 pixels of animal blown up to 640 -- not a rendering problem, and not a judgement any person or model can make. Asking for one is worse than skipping it: a coin-flip 'not a dog' can turn the whole frame into a detector negative. Off by default (0), so a fresh clone behaves exactly as it did before this existed.
_review_dup_bits: Hamming distance between two 64-bit dHashes at which the review page treats them as the same picture and shows only one. 0, the default, is exact-match only; -1 turns the collapse off. Measured twice: every duplicate that survived the sequence collapse sat at distance 0 -- one photo reached through two Mapillary sequences -- and both pairs found at 6 were wrong on sight. These crops are small and low-contrast, which is where a perceptual hash is weakest, so a generous tolerance here hides a crop nobody has judged.
triage_python: <path to a python with torch and transformers, for the crop guesser>
_llm_page: Whether the experimental LLM annotator is part of the dashboard. False, the default, removes it completely: no link in the header and no route claimed, so /llm answers 404. Nothing is deleted -- tools/dashboard/llm_page.py, tools/detect/llm_annotate.py, their guard and every answer already collected under data/llm_annotations stay exactly as they are, and setting this true brings the page back unchanged. The header is baked when the page is built, so restoring it needs a rebuild as well as a restart: set the key, run `dashboard.py build`, then restart the service. Its answers were never annotations and are not one now -- they live in their own tier and nothing that assembles a dataset reads them.
_triage_watch: Seconds the guesser sleeps between passes when the dashboard starts it. It keeps going rather than exiting: the live pool turns over at ~2 crops/s, so a single pass leaves the queue partly unguessed within the hour. Default 300.
_rfdetr_python: Interpreter for the RF-DETR guesser. A third environment on purpose: RF-DETR wants transformers>=5 and the SigLIP backend does not run on that, so installing them together breaks the one that works. Unset, the backend is not offered.
_rfdetr_model: Which RF-DETR size that backend runs: 'rfdetr' (medium, the default), 'rfdetr-small', 'rfdetr-nano' or 'rfdetr-large'.
_dogbin_python: Interpreter for the dog-bin gate -- ultralytics, a third environment again. Two features want it: the dog-bin backend of the review page's guesser, which also needs a promoted checkpoint in data/best_models.json, and the Start/Stop controls for the gate and leash passes over the whole crop store. Unset, the backend is not offered and the run controls say which key to set. The weights are NOT config: the promoted checkpoint is already recorded in data/best_models.json, and a second place to write it down is a second place for it to go stale.
